resolutions.researcher_notes: StartYear1=2028 supported by two independent sources. SICIM (Package 14 Shoaiba EPC contractor's own project page) lists 'END OF WORK 2028'; blackridgeresearch states overall MGS-3 completion Q4 2028. Construction began Q2 2024, start-up/completion 2028 — consistent. Original Aramco press release cited in sheet (aramcos-strategic-gas-expansion-progresses-with-25bn-contract-awards) currently times out; replaced with contractor + trade sources.

Sheet value Diameter='56,10,16' in. blackridgeresearch scope table quotes Package 14 Shoaiba as 'Lay various diameter lateral pipelines (56-inch, 16-inch, 10-inch) in the Shoaiba cluster (212 km)' — exact match to 56/10/16. MEED (contractors article) also reports 56-inch, 16-inch and 10-inch laterals over 212km in Shoaiba. Marked independent=false because blackridge appears to paraphrase the same MEED trade reporting. VALUE CONTRADICTION TO FLAG: the SICIM contractor page (same Package 14) lists '56-inch, 10-inch and 18-inch' — i.e. 18-inch rather than 16-inch for the third diameter. Two trade sources back 16-inch (matching sheet); the EPC contractor's own page says 18-inch. Worth a human check of which third-diameter figure is correct.

Start/End country = Saudi Arabia. Two independent JV-partner sources place Package 14 (Shoaiba segment) in the 'Shoaiba area, Kingdom of Saudi Arabia': SICIM (states 'Kingdom of Saudi Arabia', Shoaiba, 212 km) and Nesma & Partners (212 km of pipelines in the Shoaiba area, MGS-3). Shoaiba is a Saudi Red Sea coastal cluster in Makkah Province, so Saudi Arabia for both endpoints is well supported.

Owner1=Aramco 100%. SICIM names its client as 'SAUDI ARAMCO' for the MGS-3 Package 14 EPC; JPT/SPE reports Aramco awarded the $25bn of MGS-3 / Jafurah contracts as project owner. Master Gas System is a wholly Aramco-owned network. Two independent sources confirm sole Aramco ownership. (Dead Aramco press release replaced.)
